game.name: Magicite
game.short_description: Explore, craft, and survive in this Multiplayer RPG Platformer with permanent death! Featuring many Rogue-like elements, Magicite randomly generates each underground dungeon for you and your friends to delve deep into.

commentary.label: Tier list Part 1 (2023)
commentary.summary: Magicite (2014) is an older survival-exploration roguelike where you create a character, get dropped into a world, and explore to gain stronger gear in order to save the world. He was excited to try it because he had played the developer's later game. He respects it as a hardcore, historically influential title but found it slow and grindy, and got tired of it after a short play. He says he would be more likely to play it than Exit the Gungeon, but does not state a tier letter.
praise: Dropping into the world and discovering things yourself feels great
Lots of secrets and a wide variety of builds
Helped influence many roguelikes made today
criticism: Without looking things up you get stranded for a while
Random deaths lose your character and force a restart from scratch
He got tired of it after playing only a little
unique_points: Heavy reliance on hidden secrets and builds that are hard to discover without outside help
Survival-exploration structure with character loss on death, typical of older hardcore roguelikes
commentary.quote: I got tired of it slow it's grindy
design_criteria: Discovery/secrets: rewarding to find but punishing without a guide
Permadeath/character loss: restarting from scratch feels rough
Build variety: a ton of builds available
Historical influence: inspired later roguelike designers

community.one_liner: A 2D pixel-art side-scrolling RPG platformer by solo dev Sean Young (SmashGames) with permadeath, randomly generated underground dungeons, combine-any-two-items crafting and local/online co-op.
community.consensus_summary: Steam players rate it Very Positive (about 85% of roughly 7.6k reviews) and many describe it as a charming, replayable, challenging roguelite with great music and crafting. The big caveat is that development stopped years ago, and the late updates left game-breaking bugs (final-boss/victory-screen crashes, chicken cooking freezing the game, multiplayer false-loss bugs). A vocal share of the negative reviews are about abandonment and the developer's shift to Roguelands rather than the core design. No professional critic coverage exists (no Metacritic critic score, no OpenCritic entry found); Metacritic has only a small user score (7.3 from 32 ratings). A community fan patch and a 'Rewritten' project keep interest alive, but the player count is tiny (around 12-13 concurrent).
best_things: Addictive 'one more run' loop: each death leaves you slightly stronger through unlocks, giving clear short-term goals
Crafting by combining any two items is fun to experiment with and rewards discovery
High replayability through unlockable races, hats, companions and randomised stats/builds
Satisfying, challenging difficulty with a real sense of accomplishment on beating the final scourge levels
Excellent music and sound design, plus charming pixel sprites
Co-op where the run continues as long as one party member survives encourages teamwork
Good pacing, enemy and map variety; fast, ninja-like movement and combat
Strong nostalgia and loyalty among long-time players, some calling it a childhood favourite
worst_things: Abandoned: no official updates for years, with the developer having moved on to Roguelands
Late-game bugs that can make the game unwinnable, such as crashes at the final boss or victory screen
Specific known bugs: cooking raw chicken freezes the game, forced wolf riding with no jump-off, shopkeeper interaction icon disappearing
Multiplayer is buggy: false 'all players downed' game overs, players falling through the floor on restart, desyncs
Multiplayer lacks Steam integration and in-game communication tools, so people rely on third-party workarounds
Mouse cursor flicker bug reported since 2021 and never fixed
Some players consider it overpriced or mediocre compared to many modern roguelites
Some unlocks are obscure and hard to figure out
improvements: Add a tutorial or early guidance; new players get little direction on doors, recipes or systems
Let players choose their starting attributes instead of repeatedly clicking 'roll stats'
Save discovered crafting recipes so players don't have to write them down
Fix the long-standing game-breaking bugs (final boss crash, chicken cooking, multiplayer false losses)
Add Steam-integrated online multiplayer and communication tools
unique_things: Combine-any-two-items crafting as the core progression system rather than fixed recipe trees
Side-scrolling Terraria/Spelunky-style platforming blended with RPG stats, races, hats and companions
Co-op permadeath where the run only ends when the whole party is down
Inspired by Monster Hunter and Spelunky per the store description, unusual for a 2D pixel roguelite
Persistent unlocks (races, hats, companions) that change how each run plays
Active community-made fixes (MagiciteFanPatches, Magicite: Rewritten) extending the life of an abandoned game
tedious_or_disliked: Repeatedly rerolling stats until a desirable combination appears
Early game feels punishing and opaque until the mechanics click
Writing down crafting recipes because the game doesn't record them
Hunting for unlock conditions that are not explained
Working around broken bugs (shopkeepers, wolf mount) mid-run
Co-op sessions ending in frustrating false-loss resets
divisive_points: Value: fans say it is a hidden gem worth it despite bugs, while others call it abandonware to avoid at full price
Difficulty: described both as infuriating and as deeply satisfying
Multiplayer: some love the co-op, others find it the most frustrating and buggiest part (and it is local/3rd-party rather than Steam-integrated)
Reviewers disagree on whether abandonment should drag down a game they otherwise enjoy (several negative reviews are explicitly about the developer rather than the gameplay)
community.reception_notes: Launched June 9, 2014 (Steam, $9.99, Win/Mac/Linux) and built an enduring audience, with a Very Positive Steam rating that has held even as the review count grew past 7.5k. The developer stopped supporting it years ago to work on Roguelands, and players say the final update introduced game-breaking bugs, which fuels many recent negative reviews and some resentment toward the developer. The community is small but still active on Steam forums (matchmaking threads, 'Anyone still plays?' posts), with unofficial fixes like MagiciteFanPatches and a 'Magicite: Rewritten' effort. Metacritic shows only a small user score (7.3/10 from 32 ratings, no critic reviews). Note: my WebSearch budget was exhausted so no Reddit or outlet reviews could be read; Reddit and Fandom wiki fetches were blocked. Estimated sales figures come from third-party models and are not audited; the revenue calculator gave no explicit copy count (price math suggests roughly 200k+ units, but that conflicts with SteamSpy's 500k-1M owner estimate, which likely includes keys, bundles and free copies).
